steps.text: Beat sugar and softened butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth.
Beat in eggs and vanilla. Stir in flour, baking powder, and salt. Cover, and chill dough for at least 1 hour (or overnight).
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly dust a work surface with flour. Roll out dough to 1/4 to 1/2 inch thickness.
Cut into shapes with any cookie cutter. Place cookies 1 inch apart on ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until cookies are lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Carefully transfer cookies to a wire rack and cool completely before decorating.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is excellent for its purpose of rolling and cutting cookies...i tried another sugar cookie recipe and hated it...it didnt roll and cut as well and the cookies were flat and crispy...

i always come back to this one...

this year i made ghosts for my son's halloween party/parade and a friend of my daughter's birthday is on halloween so i made him a cookie bouquet using this recipe....

these cookies make GREAT cookie bouquets...

I add an additional cup of sugar and tsp of vanilla and my family liked them a LOT better...it didnt seem to affect the way they cooked either so that was good...this is still the best sugar cookie recipe ever for cutting out shapes and making cookie bouquets!! 

NOTE: i live in south florida where the heat and humidity is high - i always add between 1/4 - 1/2 cup more flour to all my cookie recipes 

Another NOTE: ....the dough, as you're rolling this particular recipe out does tend to be sticky ....simply keep dusting it with powdered sugar and you can continue to work with it...while adding additional flavor...

Thanks!

I made these for my boyfriend on our anniversary. WOW! These were it. As an aspiring pastry chef, I am always in search of great recipes and ways to "doctor them" . I made 1/4 of the batch the first time and thought they were a tad bland. SO when I made the full recipe.... I added 1/2 zest of one lemon, and 1 c. confectioner's sugar, and 1 c. granulated, for sweetness (10x sugar has more sugar per cup)creamed it with the butter, and added 2 tsp. vanilla and I followed the rest of the ingredients and instructions ...and they were exactly what I was looking for... these are THE COOKIE BOUQUET COOKIES! The only thing is you only get 20 or so cookies if you want them 1/2" thick...so I would double the recipe.

I have made this recipe too many times to count! I don't know what went wrong with those that didn't like it. My advice: FOLLOW the suggestions of others. I read through MANY reviews and this is what I got: 1.) Add in 1 more cup of sugar and 1 more tsp. vanilla. 2.) Let the dough chill overnight (saves you from frustrations) 3.) leave your bowl of dough in the fridge and just take out the portions you are working on. 4.) Use parchment paper when cutting out shapes. You will need confectioners sugar, or white sugar, or more flour when rolling out your dough. 5.) My NEW suggestion is, after cutting my cookies out, and removing the excess dough, I leave the cut outs on the parchment paper and place the whole thing in the freezer for a few minutes. When they are stiff enough to handle I place them in a air tight container and let them sit in the freezer overnight or at least a few hrs. Since it only takes a few minutes to stiffen I rotate between 2-3 pieces of paper (gotta conserve!) I cook them straight out of the freezer. It makes handling them a breeze and they keep their shape significantly better when done this way. Warning: you will obviously need to plan things out when making them. I guarantee the results are worth it!!!! As another viewer remarked: they come out as good (I think BETTER) than the cookies in the mall! I have had people trying to pay me to make them orders!!! Good Luck.....Cook-on!

There were tons of positive reviews, but I like to read the negative ones so I know what to watch out for. In this recipe, the negative reviews all said the cookies were too bland, to flour-y, and the dough was too sticky. So I chose to eliminate one of the eggs and one cup of the flour to see if I could produce a more sugary, buttery cookie. My results were as close to perfect as you could get. Even my 2.5 year-old was able to help me roll out the dough (his favorite part was flouring the rolling pin and the table!), and cut out the shapes. The dough kept its integrity through 3 rounds of re-rolling the scraps and cutting out new cookies--without having to be re-chilled. They baked perfectly (I used parchment paper on my cookie sheets) and were tender and lovely. I don't even think we'll frost them--they're that good. Though they baked so perfectly, frosting them would be easy. With my modifications, I'll never be tempted to even try another sugar cookie recipe.

I've made these sugar cookies at least a dozen times. It is a versatile dough for rolling out and making festive shapes. I have used different extracts besides vanilla including lemon, almond and maple is great for Thanksgiving leaf cookie cutters. Adding citrus zest also enhances the flavor of these cookies. I have used royal icing on baked cold cookies to decorate or a baste of egg white and sugar crystals before baking. One thing I have learned that is crucial in baking anything is measuring accurately. In order to be positive you're being accurate I have found a scale to be invaluable. This recipe assumes you are cutting out 2 inch shapes therefore the time in the oven is accurate. If you are using four inch cookie cutters extend that time to 12 to 13 minutes.

I made these with our kids for Christmas this year. I substituted King Arthur’s gluten free flour (GF) and it was a perfect result, just replace 1-to-1. Since GF food needs a little extra love, I added an extra little splash of vanilla and a little extra sugar. I mixed the wet and dry ingredients separately then stirred the flour mix into the wet ingredients. In previous attempts I used GF flour to roll out the cookies and they baked up a little dry and flavorless. This year I used others’ suggestion and rolled the dough our with powdered sugar. That made all the difference, especially with GF cookies! The cookies are soft, a little chewy, with a nice buttery flavor and a hint of vanilla and sugar. They are good on their own, but, of course, everything is better with sprinkles or colored sugar on top! We did put icing on some, but that’s another recipe that didn’t turn out quite right this year.

Recipe worked perfectly! Used a combo of salted and unsalted butter, and it didn't affect the taste whatsoever. Used a Kitchen Aid mixer and it was a tremendous help to cream the butter and sugar. Parchment paper worked well, and played with bake times to make soft vs. crispy cookies (8-9 min if cookies are thin, 10 min for thicker cookies). Overall I will be using this recipe every year!!

I like that this recipe only calls for ingredients I always have on hand. I added 1/4 tsp almond extract as well as the vanilla called for, which really made the butter flavor pop. I then chilled the dough overnight in wrapped logs and used a cheese slicer to cut round cookies that I topped with sparkling sugar crystals. I found they needed to bake 9 minutes when cut 3/8 inch thick.

Excellent recipe! Followed directions as written and also added 1 cup of diced up dried cranberries and the zest of one orange. Delicious! Rolled out nicely and dough kept the shape of the cutouts no problem. I did use powdered sugar instead of flour when dusting the counter and rolling pin though. Helps to keep the taste nice and bright instead of bogging it down with extra flour. A new favourite!

Tried & True recipe!! I have used this recipe for 8 years! This is the only rolled sugar cookie recipe I will use. I roll my dough out with a mixture of flour & granulated sugar, and it works great. Also, after I used my cookie cutter, I place them on cookie sheet & pop in the freezer for a few minutes just before putting them in oven. I bake for approximately 8.5 minutes for regular sized cookies & I bake for 6 minutes mini cookies (mini pic included, just waiting for kiddos to decorate) Happy Baking!

LOVE this recipe. But you must follow the suggestions of others, and me, lol! 1 additional cup of sugar, 1 additional cup of flour, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, 2 tsp 1, vanilla ext, and 1 tsp almond ext. Refrigerating overnight is absolutely necessary. I tried with about 8 hours and still a no go. Also rolling on parchment with powdered sugar instead of flour does wonders!

The recipe was great it was easy to make and it was easy to follow. It didn't take long to make and it was easy to bake, it didn't take long to bake and the icing I chose was a breeze to make and it was great
Easy, delicious recipe. I just wanted plain sugar cookies (no icing) so I upped the sugar just a tad, dropped spoonfuls onto a cookie sheet, and flattened them with my fingers. Wonderful!
Easy and tasty!

I have made several recipes for sugar cookies but this recipe is hands down my new go to!! I did add a bit more vanilla and a sprinkle of nutmeg to give it a bit more flavor but the dough is so easy to work with once it's cooled, I was skeptical at 1st because when I first made it it was so sticky, but trust the process!
Easy to make and comes out perfect when tips and instructions are followed. Perfectly sweet without frosting. Tip: smaller cookies = less time
Once I made this recipe I fell in love!! It is the best & tastiest sugar cookie ever! They are sweet even without frosting!! I have used it over & over for all seasons. They freeze well too!
wow
